canonical_definition: Hallucination is the tendency of a system to generate responses containing unverifiable, unsupported, or factually incorrect claims, often operationalized through unanswerable questions or adversarial benchmarks to measure severity. It manifests in text or multimodal outputs (e.g., fabricated visual elements) and is assessed via metrics like hallucination rate (e.g., contradictory/unverifiable sentence labels) or detection frameworks leveraging retrieval-augmented generation, preference optimization, or internal representation analysis. This behavior reflects risks to reliability and trustworthiness in real-world applications, with mitigation strategies including improved retriever recall, model scaling, and architectural enhancements to reduce object/attribute hallucination in vision-language tasks.
